text: Claim: \(V\) has a basis \(z_1,\dots,z_s\) such that every \(V_j\), every \(V_j\cap K\) and every \(V_j\cap K'\) is spanned by a subset of it. By downward induction on \(j\), as in the proof of Theorem 6.9, let \(B_{j+1}\) be a basis of \(V_{j+1}\) such that \(B_{j+1}\cap K\) and \(B_{j+1}\cap K'\) are bases of \(V_{j+1}\cap K\) and \(V_{j+1}\cap K'\). Complete \(B_{j+1}\cap K\) by a set \(C_1\subset V_j\cap K\) to a basis of \(V_j\cap K\); then complete \((B_{j+1}\cap K')\cup C_1\) by a set \(C_2\subset V_j\cap K'\) to a basis of \(V_j\cap K'\); finally complete \(B_{j+1}\cup C_1\cup C_2\) by a set \(D\) to a basis \(B_j\) of \(V_j\). Each step is possible. First, \(\langle C_1\rangle\cap V_{j+1}\subseteq V_{j+1}\cap K=\langle B_{j+1}\cap K\rangle\), which meets \(\langle C_1\rangle\) trivially, so \(B_{j+1}\cup C_1\) is linearly independent. Second, \(\langle B_{j+1}\cup C_1\rangle\cap K'=\langle(B_{j+1}\cap K')\cup C_1\rangle\): if \(b+c\in K'\) with \(b\in V_{j+1}\) and \(c\in\langle C_1\rangle\subseteq K'\), then \(b\in V_{j+1}\cap K'=\langle B_{j+1}\cap K'\rangle\); so \(B_{j+1}\cup C_1\cup C_2\) is linearly independent. No element of \(C_2\) lies in \(K\) and no element of \(D\) lies in \(K'\), since otherwise independence would fail; so \(B_j\cap K\) and \(B_j\cap K'\) are bases of \(V_j\cap K\) and \(V_j\cap K'\). The basis \(B_0\) proves the claim.

(2) The \(u\)-part. Let \(i<j\), so \(d(i)\le d(j)\); the term is \(u_{ij}q_{ij}[Y_i,x_j]\). If \(d(i)=d(j)=3\), then \(u_{ij}=3u'_{ij}\) by (c1) and \(3[Y_i,x_j]=[Y_i,x_j^3]=[Y_i,Y_j]\) by (I4); this vanishes if \(i\) or \(j\) lies in \(N_3\), as \([\gamma_3,\gamma_2]=1\). In \((\ast)\) with \(d(i)=3\) the right side is \(\equiv0\pmod3\): for \(h<i\) we have \(d(h)=3\) and \(3\mid u_{hi}\) by (c1), and the terms of \(E^w_i\) vanish modulo \(3\) by (c3) and (c5). Let \(\gamma_4\) have exponent \(9\), for instance \(\gamma_4\cong C_9\). Then still \(T_5=0\), as \(d(i)\mid\binom{d(i)}2\) and \([R_i,x_i,x_i]^{d(i)}=[[R_i,x_i],Y_i]=1\) by (K4). Each argument of step (4) for \(T_1,\dots,T_4\) still gives a factor \(3\) in front of a value of \(\omega\) or \(t\), so these terms lie in \(\gamma_4^3\), and so does \(g\), in accordance with Corollary 6.12; but they need not vanish. The terms with an index of order \(3\) do vanish: the relevant value of \(\omega\) or \(t\) is then killed by \(3\) (for \(T_1\) with \(d(i)=3\) and \(T_4\) with \(d(j)=3\) because \(3\bar c=0\); for \(T_2\) with \(d(i)=3\) and \(T_3\) with \(d(i)=3\) by (K4)), and for \(T_2\) with \(d(h)=3\), \(d(i)=9\) one uses \([Y_h,x_i,x_i]=[c_{hi},x_i]^3\), from (K2), so that the term is \(-u_{hi}[c_{hi},x_i]^9=-u_{hi}\,\omega(\bar c_{hi},\bar Y_i)\) by (K3) (the \(t\)-term is killed by \(3\), as \(3\bar c_{hi}=0\)), which vanishes by (c2) if \(i\in A\) and as \(\bar Y_i\in3L_2\) if \(i\in N\) (for \(d(i)\ge27\), \(9\mid q_{hi}\)). What remains are terms \(3\cdot(\text{a value of }\omega\text{ or }t)\in\gamma_4^3\) (\(\cong C_3\) when \(\gamma_4\cong C_9\)) on generators \(x_i\) of order \(\ge9\) modulo \(\gamma_2\): \(T_1\) for \(9\le d(i)\le d(h)\), \(T_2\) for \(d(h)\ge9\), \(T_3\) for \(d(i)\ge9\), \(T_4\) for \(d(j)\ge9\). To kill them one would need information not used here, e.g. (A), (C\(_2\))–(C\(_4\)), (D\(_1\)), (F\(_1\)), (B) and (D\(_2\)) modulo \(9\), or the row \(h\) of (E) paired with other \(x_m\). Computations: in the \(661\) groups of the check after Theorem 6.11 with \(\gamma_4\) of exponent \(9\) (\(531\) of them with \(\gamma_4\cong C_9\) and cyclic centre) every term \(T_1,\dots,T_5\) is trivial on the lattice of admissible families in the adapted basis, which is more than is proved here. Independently, the truncated Magnus algebra (with the exactness certificate; the control \(z\in D_4\) holds in all) gives \(D_5=1\) in \(940\) random groups of class \(4\) with \(\gamma_4\cong C_9\), cyclic centre, \(\gamma_2/\gamma_3\) of exponent \(9\) or \(27\) and \(Q_{ab}\) of types \([9,9,3]\), \([9,9,3,3]\), \([9,9,9]\), \([9,9,9,3]\), \([27,9,3]\), \([27,9,3,3]\), \([27,27,3]\) or \([27,27,3,3]\), of orders \(3^{11}\)–\(3^{26}\), \(287\) of them with \(\gamma_2^9\not\subseteq\gamma_4\): the generator \(z\) of \(\Omega_1(Z)=\gamma_4^3\) does not lie in \(D_5\) (so \(D_5=1\), as a nontrivial normal subgroup meets the cyclic centre), and the solver of Tahara's conditions gives \(g=1\) in all of them.
